primary.title: The Gathas
primary.author: Zoroaster
primary.rationale: The Gathas are the oldest hymns of Zoroastrianism, believed to have been composed by Zoroaster himself. They are central to understanding his teachings.

primary.title: Avesta
primary.author: Zoroaster
primary.rationale: While the Avesta is a collection of Zoroastrian scriptures, the Gathas within it are attributed to Zoroaster. Other parts may contain his teachings or traditions derived from him.

secondary.title: Zoroastrianism: An Introduction
secondary.author: Jenny Rose
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and accessible introduction to Zoroastrianism, covering its history, beliefs, and practices, with significant attention to Zoroaster.

secondary.title: The Zoroastrian Flame: Its Origins, Philosophy, and Ritual
secondary.author: R.C. Zaehner
secondary.rationale: A foundational scholarly work that delves into the origins and philosophical underpinnings of Zoroastrianism, offering insights into Zoroaster's role.

secondary.title: Zoroaster's Influence on Greek Thought
secondary.author: Shaul Shaked
secondary.rationale: This article explores the historical influence of Zoroaster's ideas on later philosophical traditions, providing context for his significance.

suggestions.notes: Dating Zoroaster and his works is highly debated among scholars. The Gathas are considered his most authentic utterances. Primary sources are often part of larger collections like the Avesta.
